name: Adjust bicycle brakes
blurb: Brakes that bite properly, with pads centred and cables tensioned, are both a safety issue and a five-minute job with basic tools.
gear: A 5 mm hex and a cable cutter if replacing cables
Rubbing alcohol for rotors, if disc brakes
steps: Identify your brake type: rim, mechanical disc or hydraulic disc — the adjustments differ.
For rim brakes, check the pads: they should contact the braking surface squarely, not the tyre, with a slight toe-in at the front.
Set cable tension with the barrel adjuster so the lever engages firmly a third of the way through its travel, well before it reaches the bar.
Centre the calliper so both pads clear the rim equally, using the centring screw or by adjusting the mounting bolt.
For mechanical discs, adjust the fixed pad first, then the cable, aiming for a rotor that spins free but stops fast.
Test at walking pace before you trust them, and check pad wear regularly.
tips: Never let oil or degreaser touch a disc rotor or pad. Contaminated pads are only fixable by replacement.
A lever that reaches the handlebar is dangerous, not merely soft. Fix it before riding.
proof: Both brakes stop the bike firmly with a solid lever feel and no rubbing when released.
